what_matters.tag_note: Meta · results after Wednesday's US close
what_matters.head: Meta's revenue beat its own forecast, but a $9.9B legal charge cut earnings per share to $3.83, against the $5.46 analysts expected. The shares rose 2.1% after hours.
what_matters.detail: Revenue was $64.6B, up 26%, above the company's $61–64B forecast. The charge is for Meta's settlement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental health; Meta raised its 2026 expense forecast to $175–179B to take it. It narrowed its 2026 spending plan for data centres and equipment to $135–145B (was $130–145B) and gave no 2027 figure. Free cash flow was negative, at −$2.1B, and it bought back no shares. Fourth-quarter revenue forecast: $73–76B. Separately, during Wednesday's trading a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25B in the Cambridge Analytica privacy case; the state had asked for $35–40B and Meta for at most $3.45B. Meta says it will appeal. The shares closed 0.5% higher.

what_matters.head: SK Hynix fell 4.5% and Samsung 3.8% in Seoul by 13:05 local time, although US chip stocks rose overnight.
what_matters.detail: Investing.com tied the Asian sell-off to mixed US tech results that did not reassure investors about returns on AI spending. Lam Research, not held, beat forecasts with its results on Wednesday but fell about 6% after hours; Korea was 20% of its sales in the quarter. Both Seoul moves are about 0.6× usual. SK Hynix is 29% lower than a month ago and reports on 28 Oct.

what_matters.tag_note: Nokia out · Bloom Energy and Western Digital tonight
what_matters.head: Nokia's results came out at 13:00 SGT, after the run: sales rose 10% to €5.15B, and sales to AI and cloud customers rose 123% from a year earlier.
what_matters.detail: Orders from those customers rose 118%; the reports read gave no euro figure for either. Comparable operating margin rose to 11.7% from 9.5%. Nokia kept its 2026 comparable operating profit forecast of €2.1–2.6B and expects fourth-quarter sales 20–24% above the third's. Not in any price above. Tonight after the New York close: Bloom Energy (about 04:05 SGT Friday) and Western Digital, not held (call 04:30 SGT).

after_data.text: Yemen's Houthis struck several targets in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday: a drone attack on an oil field killed two people, and at least one person was killed at Dammam's civilian airport. The US ordered some diplomats and family members to leave its missions in the kingdom. Brent was $110.11 at 08:34 SGT, up 1.2% (Reuters). The oil-field report came after Wednesday's oil settlement, so it is not in the oil figure above (Yahoo Finance).

Tesla, not held, cut its capital-spending forecast with its results after Wednesday's close, and its shares fell 3.3% after hours. In Asian trade, Nasdaq 100 futures were down 1.7% and S&P 500 futures 0.9% (Investing.com). Not in Wednesday's US prices.

Micron's Taoyuan union began a 24-hour strike at the plant gate at 09:00 today, running to 09:00 Friday, after talks on Wednesday produced no figures on bonuses or profit-sharing. The union said it would put the offer Micron was due to present at a 10:00 staff meeting to a member vote. Turnout and any effect on output had not been reported (Economic Daily; udn.com). The Taichung union signed an agreement with Micron on Wednesday; its terms have not been published (Focus Taiwan).

latest.tape_note: US stocks rose on Wednesday: the S&P 500 gained about 0.6%, the Nasdaq 1% and the Dow 0.7%. Yahoo Finance tied the rise to SpaceX's results reviving interest in AI stocks, and chipmakers led: the chip fund rose 2.1%. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 3 basis points to 5.15%, and VIX fell to 16.7. Brent settled little changed and US crude lower (Reuters); the attacks on Saudi Arabia are in After the data.

recent.headline: Meta's revenue beat its own forecast, but a $9.9B legal charge cut earnings per share to $3.83, against the $5.46 analysts expected. The shares rose 2.1% after hours.
After Tuesday's US close, Super Micro raised its estimate of last quarter's revenue to $18.5–19.5B, from its forecast of $14.5–15.5B, citing demand for AI platforms.
Chip stocks fell for a ninth straight session on Friday. The iShares chip fund lost 4.1% on the day and 16.3% across the nine sessions, and software stocks fell with them.
Aixtron fell 12.7% in Frankfurt on Thursday, 3.3 times its usual day. Half an hour after the close it said its third-quarter orders and profit were well above expectations.

Chip and AI stocks fell hard on Wednesday. US consumer prices rose more than expected in September, which raised bets on another Fed rate rise, and worries about how AI data centres are paid for spread.
